title: Russia Sanctions: EU Targets Oil & Banks, Stablecoin Bill Boosts Crypto | Bloomberg The Pulse 7/18
content:
European Union states have approved a fresh sanctions package on Russia over its war against Ukraine including a revised oil price cap, new banking restrictions, and curbs on fuels made from Russian petroleum. The package, the bloc’s 18th since Moscow’s full scale invasion, will see about 20 more Russian banks cut off the international payments system SWIFT and face a full transaction ban, as well as restrictions imposed on Russian petroleum refined in third countries. A large oil refinery in India, part-owned by Russia’s state-run oil company, Rosneft, was also blacklisted. 

Today's guests: Eelco Heinen, Dutch Finance Minister, Matheus Dibo, Goldman Sachs Private Wealth Management Investment Strategy Group Managing Director, Marcus Garvey, Macquarie Head of Commodities Strategy, Sanusha Naidu, Institute for Global Dialogue Senior Research Fellow (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crypto Market Cap Hits $4 Trillion as US Passes Stablecoin Bill | The Opening Trade 07/18
content:
Congress delivered a watershed victory for the crypto industry on Thursday, passing the first federal legislation to regulate stablecoins and clearing the way for broader use of the technology in everyday finance.

Backed by Republicans and championed by President Donald Trump, the bill imposes federal or state oversight on dollar-linked tokens that can move around the clock and across platforms. Supporters say it could unlock faster, cheaper forms of payments — and bring legitimacy to a $265 billion market that Citigroup Inc. analysts expect could swell to $3.7 trillion by 2030.

content: South Africa is edging closer to leaving a global financial watchdog’s so-called gray list in October, with a team of assessors scheduled to visit the nation this month.

title: Powell Letter Addresses White House Criticism of Fed Renovations
content: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell in a Thursday letter countered criticisms leveled at the central bank by a top White House official over a $2.5 billion renovation project.

title: Senegal, Saudi Partner Ink New Desalination-Plant Deal After Cost Review
content: Senegal reached a new agreement with Saudi Arabia’s Acwa Power to proceed with a desalination plant after a cost review, President Bassirou Diomaye Faye said.

title: Colombia Central Banker Flags Peso Rally Risk to Rate Outlook
content: Colombia’s central bank is scrutinizing the peso’s surge to determine whether the rally reflects solid fundamentals or speculative inflows, one of its newest board members said in an interview.

title: Italy’s Giorgetti Is Worrying About Fallout From the Trade War
content: Italian Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said he’s concerned about potential damage to European economies from trade tensions and the weakening of the US dollar.

title: Fiscal Discipline Faces Another Downgrade in Japan’s Election
content: I’m Chris Anstey, an economics editor in Boston. Today we’re looking at the economic policy implications of Sunday’s election in Japan. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so  here.

title: ECB Seen Opting for Lending Tools Over QE in Future Crises
content: The European Central Bank will pick lending to banks over bond-buying in almost all future situations that require unconventional responses, according to a Bloomberg poll of economists.

title: EU Agrees to Start Talks With Gulf Nations on Strategic Ties
content: European Union member states approved the launch of negotiations with six Gulf countries as the bloc seeks to broaden its international partnerships amid tariff threats from President Donald Trump.

title: Challenges to Fed Independence Resonate Beyond US, Nagel Says
content: Interference in the independence of the Federal Reserve would be felt outside of the US, according to Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel.

title: Thai Finance Chief Sees US Cutting 36% Tariff on Fresh Proposal
content: Thailand expects the US to reduce a threatened tariff on its exports from 36% to a level in line with regional neighbors after presenting a “very substantial improvement” in a fresh round of talks, Finance Minister Pichai Chunhavajira said.

title: Malaysian Growth Unexpectedly Quickens Despite Trade Risks
content: Malaysia’s economy grew faster than expected in the second quarter, driven by the services sector, even as the country contends with US President Donald Trump’s rollout of global tariffs.

title: Japan Official Urges China to Expand Foreign Investment Quota
content: A Japanese government official called on China to expand a program allowing certain mainland investors to put more money abroad, citing “strong enthusiasm” for Japanese stocks.

title: A Rebel Army Is Building a Rare-Earth Empire on China’s Border
content: The Kachin Independence Organization fought for decades in obscurity. Now it’s supplying essential minerals to manufacturers around the world.

title: ECB Can Afford to Wait Until December to Make Final Rate Cut, Survey Shows
content: The European Central Bank can delay its final interest-rate cut until December without investors concluding in the meantime that easing is over, a Bloomberg survey of economists showed.

title: Japan’s Inflation Stays Elevated After Easing From Two-Year High
content: Japan’s key price measure cooled a tad more than expected while remaining well above the Bank of Japan’s target, keeping pressure on Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba to mollify voters as he heads into Sunday’s national election.

title: Waller Says Fed Should Cut Rates Now With Labor Market on Edge
content: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers should cut interest rates this month to support a labor market that is showing signs of weakness.

title: Milei Wins Second Upgrade by Moody’s on Easing FX Controls
content: Argentina’s credit rating was upgraded by Moody’s Ratings for a second time this year, with the agency citing the easing of currency controls and support from the International Monetary Fund.

title: Trump’s Trade War Is Upending China’s Factory Floors
content: As chaotic tariff negotiations disrupt global supply chains and make planning more difficult, manufacturers in China are racing to adapt.

title: Hungary’s Biggest Bank CEO Calls for Euro Adoption and Predictability
content: The new chief executive officer of Hungary’s largest lender called for the adoption of the euro and for an end to ad-hoc policymaking under Prime Minister Viktor Orban that has sapped investor confidence and dented valuations.

title: Japan’s Ishiba Faces Tough Choices If LDP Suffers Election Blow
content: The outlook for Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba looks bleak should his ruling coalition fail to hold on to a majority in Sunday’s upper house election.

title: Debt Demands Rise in Canada as Carney Prepares More Spending
content: The supply of Canada’s government debt is set to hit a record this fiscal year as Prime Minister Mark Carney pledges to use the federal balance sheet to make investments in the economy.

title: Barclays Sees Medicaid Reductions Hurting 15 States the Most
content: President Donald Trump’s budget bill that could deeply cut the nation’s largest public health-insurance program stands to hurt some states more than others, according to Barclays Plc.

title: Daly Says Fed Shouldn’t Wait Too Long to Start Cutting Rates
content: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said she still thinks it’s reasonable for policymakers to plan on two interest-rate cuts this year, emphasizing that the central bank should not wait too long before moving.

title: G-20 Nearing Deal on Communique, S. Africa Finance Head Says
content: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said the Group of 20 nations are nearing a deal on a communique.

title: Summers Warns of ‘Massive Inflation Psychology’ From Trump Rates
content: Former Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers warned that President Donald Trump’s bid to assert control over the Federal Reserve and drive down interest rates could trigger a surge in inflation expectations that pushes up long-term borrowing costs.

title: Canada’s Finance Chief Says Tariffs Are Likely to Stick as US Talks Grind On
content: Canada’s finance minister signaled that any trade deal with the US is likely to include at least some tariffs, and repeated that the country’s dairy and poultry protections won’t be on the table during negotiations.

title: Chevron Prevails in Exxon Fight and Closes Deal to Buy Hess
content: Chevron Corp. won its arbitration battle with Exxon Mobil Corp. and has closed its $53 billion deal to buy Hess Corp. more than 20 months after the takeover was announced.

title: How Taylor Swift Turned a Glitter Freckle Maker Into a Sensation
content: A beauty company’s signature product went viral at a Chiefs game last fall. Private equity firms have been knocking on its 29-year-old co-founders’ doors ever since.

title: Amex Tops Estimates as Premium Clients Keep Up Card Spending
content: American Express Co.’s billed business on its cards and other products outperformed expectations in the second quarter as its affluent customers continued to spend.

title: Talen Buys Two Gas Power Plants in Race to Meet AI Demand
content: The rush to snap up US natural gas power plants to feed surging electric demand from data centers has resulted in the fourth big deal of the year, with Talen Energy Corp.’s $3.8 billion purchase of facilities in Pennsylvania and Ohio.

title: Schwab Earnings Top Estimates on Trading Boost, Client Assets
content: Charles Schwab Corp. reported earnings per share that topped estimates as the firm said client assets hit a new record and trading revenue rose.

title: Danske Net Interest Income Tops Estimates on Loan Demand
content: Danske Bank A/S, the largest lender in Denmark, reported better-than-expected lending income in the second quarter as brisker demand for loans offset the impact of lower deposit margins.

title: Ally Shares Climb After Earnings, Auto Lending Top Estimates
content: Ally Financial Inc. shares rose after the lender reported strong consumer auto-loan originations and earnings that topped analysts’ expectations.

title: Senegal, Saudi Partner Ink New Desalination-Plant Deal After Cost Review

title: Sarepta Sinks After Another Patient Dies on Gene Therapy
content: Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. said another patient has died from acute liver failure after receiving one of its gene therapies, putting additional pressure on the biotech company after the recent deaths of two teenage boys.

title: Porsche Plans More Cost Cuts To Counter Tariffs, China Slump
content: Porsche AG warned its employees to brace for further cost reductions as the luxury-car maker seeks ways to offset declining sales in China and the escalating cost of US tariffs.

title: HSBC Disbands Team Focused on Managing Geopolitical Risks
content: HSBC Holdings Plc is disbanding a team of staffers that were focused on identifying and managing geopolitical risk even as the possibility of such threats has ratcheted up since US President Donald Trump returned to power.

title: Netflix Tops Wall Street’s Lofty Estimates, Raises Forecast
content: While rival media companies are unloading assets and cutting costs, Netflix Inc. continues to thrive.

title: Drone Crashes, Security Threats Have States Demanding Power to Take Them Down
content: While authorities were desperately trying to save people from the deadly Fourth of July floods in Kerr County, Texas, a private drone collided with a search and rescue helicopter and forced it to make an emergency landing, one of the latest incidents in a trend of uncrewed aerial vehicles flying into restricted zones.

title: Reckitt Sells Homecare Brands to Advent in $4.8 Billion Deal
content: Reckitt Benckiser Group Plc agreed to sell most of its homecare business to private equity firm Advent International for an enterprise value of up to $4.8 billion as the UK consumer goods company focuses on faster-growing operations.

title: 3M Hikes Earnings Outlook in Boost to CEO’s Turnaround Plan

title: BP Agrees to Sell US Onshore Wind Business to LS Power
content: BP Plc agreed to sell its US onshore wind business to LS Power, as the company continues efforts to pivot back toward its core oil and gas business and reverse years of share underperformance.

content: Wells Fargo & Co. suspended travel to China after one of its top trade financing bankers was blocked from leaving the country, the latest case of authorities imposing exit bans on staff of foreign firms.

title: Swedish Industrials Prove Tariff Resilience, Flag Currency Hit
content: Sweden’s industrial companies are demonstrating resilience in the face of US President Donald Trump’s trade war, though currency headwinds are darkening their outlook.

title: Cerberus to Expand Subic Bay Business as US Interest in Former Naval Base Grows

content: Target Corp. is ending a long-standing program that matches prices of items with those of competitors, as the big-box retailer looks to simplify its pricing strategy.

content: Buy-now-pay-later providers will finally be regulated in the UK beginning next year, the Financial Conduct Authority said on Friday.

content: After developing swelling in his lower legs, President Donald Trump was diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency, a condition that develops when blood doesn’t properly flow from the legs back toward the heart.
